blocks.content: This chapter covers both Chandigarh-specific administrative initiatives and how pan-India flagship schemes have played out distinctively in the UT — a compact but regularly tested current-affairs-linked chapter.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Smart City & Urban Development focuses on sustainable urban planning, infrastructure upgrading, and civic utility management.
Housing & Welfare programs strive to deliver affordable housing options and social security benefits to targeted populations.
Transport & Connectivity projects aim to strengthen multi-modal transport networks, highways, and logistics across the country.
Digital Governance & E-Services leverage technology to make government service delivery transparent, accessible, and efficient.

Chandigarh was selected under the Government of India's Smart Cities Mission, with the Chandigarh Smart City Limited (CSCL) as the implementing special purpose vehicle, focused on integrated traffic management, smart parking, e-governance, and public Wi-Fi/surveillance infrastructure.
The UT has undertaken heritage-conservation-linked smart infrastructure works around the Capitol Complex, balancing UNESCO World Heritage obligations with modern civic upgrades.

Chandigarh's Master Plan (periodically revised, most recently referenced as 'Master Plan 2031') governs long-term zoning, density, and peripheral village/colony regularisation — a recurring subject of public consultation and Administration decision-making.

The Chandigarh Housing Board (CHB) is the UT's public housing agency, historically responsible for building much of the city's residential sector stock and continuing to run affordable-housing and slum-rehabilitation schemes.

Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Urban) has been implemented in Chandigarh for economically weaker section and low-income group housing, including in-situ slum redevelopment projects in colonies like Dhanas and Maloya.
Ayushman Bharat and the Chandigarh-specific health insurance schemes have been extended to UT residents, layered atop the UT's already strong public hospital infrastructure (GMCH-32, PGIMER).

cells: A metro rail project has been proposed and studied for the Tricity region (Chandigarh-Panchkula-Mohali) at various points, though as of the mid-2020s it remains at the planning/feasibility stage rather than under active construction — candidates should verify the latest status before an exam

Located at Mohali (Punjab side of the Tricity), inaugurated in its expanded international terminal form in 2015, serving the whole Tricity region despite being physically outside the Chandigarh UT boundary — a frequently tested 'trick' fact
The UT's public bus operator, among the earlier Indian cities to induct electric buses into its public fleet as part of the FAME/National Electric Bus programme
Well-connected rail hub linking the city to Delhi, Amritsar and other major destinations via the Shatabdi and other express trains

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Chandigarh International Airport is physically located in Mohali, Punjab — NOT within the Chandigarh UT boundary itself, despite carrying the 'Chandigarh' name. A frequently tested distinguishing fact.

items: Focus on launch dates, nodal ministries, and specific targets for major national schemes under urban and digital governance.
Memorize key transport infrastructure initiatives (e.g., Bharatmala, Sagarmala, UDAN) and their distinct operational domains.
Expect matching or statement-based questions regarding digital service portals, e-governance platforms, and housing welfare schemes.

Chandigarh has been an early and consistent high-performer in national e-governance rankings, given its small size, high literacy, and administrative capacity, with widespread rollout of online civic-service delivery (property tax, utility bills, certificates) through its Smart City digital platforms.
The UT Administration has promoted CCTV-based integrated command-and-control systems for traffic and public-safety monitoring under the Smart City programme.
Chandigarh Smart City Limited (CSCL) implements the UT's Smart Cities Mission projects.
Chandigarh International Airport is located in Mohali, Punjab, NOT inside the Chandigarh UT itself.
Chandigarh Housing Board (CHB) is the UT's public housing agency; PMAY(U) covers EWS/LIG housing including in-situ slum redevelopment.
CTU (Chandigarh Transport Undertaking) has been an early adopter of electric buses in its public fleet.
A Tricity metro rail project has been studied/proposed for Chandigarh-Panchkula-Mohali but was not under active construction as of the mid-2020s — verify current status before an exam.
